pins: the locked floor bounds the post-payout downside at exactly the buffer minus the lock offset: a day that loses all 90,000c of it closes on the floor and does not breach, and none of what was risked was ever withdrawable
note: `balance_cents` AND `floor_cents` ARE THE SAME NUMBER AND THAT IS THE FIXTURE. The account ends the maximum-variance day standing exactly on its locked floor: it has lost every cent AS-04 says is at risk and not one cent more, and `breached: false` beside them is R-21's strict `<` doing the only work it can do at that boundary. An engine that wrote `<=` closes this account. `withdrawable_cents: 0` IS THE OTHER HALF OF AS-04's CLAIM, that 'the only thing at risk post-lock is progress above size + 10,000c, which is the buffer, which was never withdrawable'. The withdrawable is 160,000c on day one, 150,000c on day two, and zero from the extraction onward, so the 90,000c day four destroys is buffer money the trader could never have taken out. `floor_locked: true` WITH `floor_cents: 5010000` IS PINNED ON A CLOSE THAT LANDS EXACTLY ON THE TRIGGER, and that is the only place in this directory where a locked floor can be pinned at all. R-15's trigger is `>=`, so a close that overshoots leaves section 3.4's `max(trailed, locked)` at 5,050,000 and section 3.6's assignment at 5,010,000, 40,000c apart on the value every later breach compares against, and M01 still says both. Day one closes at 5,260,000, which is CV-12's exact-continuity case, so the two readings coincide and this file ratifies neither. `high_water_balance_cents: 5260000` IS R-13's FREEZE, carried through three later days none of which raised it. It is pinned as the input the locked floor is derived from rather than as an independent claim: a lock that failed to freeze the high-water balance would leave this at 5,260,000 anyway on this stream, because no later close exceeds it. GS-016 is the row that discriminates that, and it is written. `win_days_count: 1` AGAINST `traded_days_count: 4` SAYS THE EXTRACTION WAS NOT EARNED IN THIS STREAM AND THE FILE IS NOT PRETENDING OTHERWISE. R-34 needs five win days on this plan. What this fixture states is a non-trading movement on a mark (R-10), which is how a settled payout reaches the fold; whether the gates permitted it is `evaluatePayout`'s question and no field here answers it. GS-065 is the file where the same 150,000c extraction is earned, over AS-03's five-win-day path, and it pins the unlocked half of R-19's loss-room sentence. ADR-052 IS PENDING SIGNATURE AND CHANGES NO FIELD HERE, WHICH WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. It rules for section 3.6's assignment against section 3.4's `max`; on a close that lands exactly on the trigger the trailed floor and the locked value are the same number, so both readings produce 5,010,000 and this file is green under either. Its CV-11 counterexample needs a lock-day close above `size + buffer + drawdown` (5,350,000 on this plan) and day one closes at 5,260,000, so this stream does not reach it either. EC-157 IS RULED AND ITS OWN ENTRY DOES NOT SAY SO. Every mark here carries a non-zero adjustment or sits after one, which EC-157 calls unwritable while `daily_marks_balance_arithmetic` stands; `0036` superseded that constraint on Repair A (2026-08-16) and the surviving CHECK is `closing = opening + realized_pnl`, which every day in this file satisfies.
